newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: US sees consensus to speed Rwandan repatriation.
newsitem.headline: US sees consensus to speed Rwandan repatriation.

text.p: Assistant U.S. Secretary of State Phyllis Oakley said on Thursday that a consensus was emerging among donor countries and in states of Africa's Great Lakes region to accelerate repatriation of 1.6 million Rwandans.
Oakley also called the deteriorating security situation in eastern Zaire, home to 1.1 million Rwandan Hutus, "worrisome".

She has been attending a week-long policy meeting of the U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) at which officials from 51 states are reviewing UNHCR proposals gradually to close the Rwandan refugee camps in Zaire and Tanzania and repatriate the inmates.
Neither the timetable, cost, nor any other details of the UNHCR draft proposals have been released.

"UNHCR has a draft on the table...I think there has been an emerging consensus," Oakley, assistant secretary of the State Department's bureau of population, refugees and migration, told a news conference in Geneva.
"Without strong disagreement from major donors, we would then expect the UNHCR to go forward," she added.
"We will certainly be continuing those discussions in capitals and trying to move that situation along."

By giving the Rwandan refugees a choice between voluntarily going home with U.N. assistance or relocating in countries of asylum, UNHCR has said it hopes to break extremists' control over the camps and their intimidation of the refugees.
The refugees are mainly Hutus who fled Rwanda in 1994 fearing reprisals after the massacre of up to a million Tutsis and Hutu moderates.
"Discussions are continuing," a UNHCR spokesman said. "We don't expect any decision in the UNHCR executive committee.
"Obviously, we want to resolve the problem. But participating officials will report back to their respective governments," he added.
